# intervals.library: ParameterOf

```plato

    // The parameter `t` for which At(self, t) equals `x` (inverse lerp): maps `x`
    // from [Start, End] back onto the unitless fraction line, so Start -> 0 and
    // End -> 1. Precondition: Start != End (a zero-width interval has no inverse).
    ParameterOf(self: NumberInterval, x: Number): Number
        => self.Start.InverseLerp(self.End, x);

    // Remap `x` from the `from` interval onto the `to` interval: the two-inverse-lerp
    // composition At(to, ParameterOf(from, x)). Every shader/UI/animation
    // normalized-coordinate remap is this one call. Precondition: from is not
    // zero-width. Unclamped — pass x within `from`, or Clamp first, to stay inside `to`.
    Remap(x: Number, from: NumberInterval, to: NumberInterval): Number
        => to[from.ParameterOf(x)];

    // The overlapping sub-interval common to `a` and `b` (interval intersection),
    // returned as a concrete NumberInterval so ray-box slab reductions can
    // chain Overlap and read Start/End directly. When the two are disjoint the result
    // is inverted (Start > End) — the empty encoding (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md -
    // Bounds); test it with IsForward. The remap-kit spelling of the generic
    // IInterval.Intersection, which returns the same NumberInterval via `Self`.
    Overlap(a: NumberInterval, b: NumberInterval): NumberInterval
        => (a.Start.Greater(b.Start), a.End.Lesser(b.End));

    //==
    // AngleInterval — a directed angular range / arc sweep (items 11, 14).
    // Convention: endpoints are INCLUSIVE and the sweep is the CCW (increasing-angle)
    // arc from Start to End, which MAY cross the +/-pi seam — an arc from 170 deg to
    // -170 deg is the short 20 deg sweep across the seam, not the long way round. The
    // wrap-aware helpers below reduce every offset into [0, one turn) via Angle.Wrap
    // (angles.library.plato) before comparing, so they are stable across the seam,
    // unlike the generic linear IInterval.Contains/Extent (which read Start<=End
    // literally and are only correct for non-wrapping ranges). Union/Intersection are
    // deliberately NOT specialized for angular ranges: the union of two circular arcs
    // is not always an arc, so no sound closed form exists on this type; consumers
    // that need a set operation must work in the reduced [0, tau) parameter space.

    // The CCW angular width of the arc, reduced to [0, one turn). Unlike the generic
    // Extent (raw End - Start, which can be negative or exceed a turn), Span is the
    // seam-stable sweep magnitude: a full-turn arc (Start == End) reads as 0.
    Span(self: AngleInterval): Angle
        => (self.End - self.Start).Wrap(1.0.Turns);

    // True when `a` lies on the CCW arc from Start to End, endpoints inclusive and
    // seam-crossing handled: `a`'s CCW offset from Start (reduced to [0, one turn))
    // must not exceed the arc's Span. Correct across the +/-pi seam, where the linear
    // IInterval.Contains is not.
    Contains(self: AngleInterval, a: Angle): Boolean
        => (a - self.Start).Wrap(1.0.Turns) <= (self.End - self.Start).Wrap(1.0.Turns);

    // The angle half way ALONG the arc: Start advanced by half the Span. This is the
    // seam-aware partner of Contains above, and it is deliberately not the generic
    // IInterval.Center (Lerp(0.5), the arithmetic mean of the stored endpoints).
    // The two agree exactly whenever the raw End - Start lies in [0, one turn), which
    // is the regime every arc consumer works in; they diverge only once the stored
    // extent wraps, and there the arithmetic mean is not on the arc at all. For
    // Start = -6.988 rad, End = 2 rad the sweep is Span = 2.705 rad, whose midpoint
    // is -5.636 rad, while the arithmetic mean -2.494 rad sits 4.494 rad along a
    // 2.705 rad arc -- outside the very arc that Span and Contains measure.
    Center(self: AngleInterval): Angle
        => self.Start + self.Span * 0.5;

    //==
    // # Derived functionality for ITransformable2D / ITransformable3D
    //
    // Bodies for the `ITransformable2D` / `ITransformable3D` interfaces declared in
    // `transforms.concepts.plato`: the ordered multi-transform convenience
    // overloads, and the lifting of every transform representation through Deform so
    // that a single Deform primitive yields a complete transform surface.

    //==
    // ITransformable2D / ITransformable3D — a value that can be carried through the
    // general transform of its dimension. The convenience overloads below are named
    // ThenTransform rather than reusing the interface's `Transform` name: overloading a
    // interface-declared member on arity alone is easy to misread, and ThenTransform
    // states the sequencing intent.

    // Apply two transforms in order: `first` then `second`. Equal to
    // Transform(first.Compose(second)) — the helper exists so the caller does not
    // have to name the composition.
    ThenTransform(self: ITransformable2D, first: Transform2D, second: Transform2D): Self
        => self.Transform(first).Transform(second);

    // Apply three transforms in order.
    ThenTransform(self: ITransformable2D, first: Transform2D, second: Transform2D, third: Transform2D): Self
        => self.Transform(first).Transform(second).Transform(third);

    // Apply two transforms in order: `first` then `second`.
    ThenTransform(self: ITransformable3D, first: Transform3D, second: Transform3D): Self
        => self.Transform(first).Transform(second);

    // Apply three transforms in order.
    ThenTransform(self: ITransformable3D, first: Transform3D, second: Transform3D, third: Transform3D): Self
        => self.Transform(first).Transform(second).Transform(third);

    // Deliberately NOT extended: an inverse-transform and a transform-about-a-pivot
    // helper would need an inverse, and a homography has none in general — its
    // matrix is singular whenever the map collapses a dimension. Identity is a
    // per-representation static (see `transforms.library.plato`), not an interface
    // member, for the same reason it is not derivable here.

    //==
    // Deform implies Transform — lifting a point map through Deform gives every
    // deformable type a complete transform surface from its single Deform primitive.
    // The `transforms-*.library.plato` files already apply each representation to a
    // bare Point2D/Point3D; lifting that point map through Deform generalizes the
    // pattern to all Deformable types. Implementing Deform for a new shape therefore
    // gives it Transform for all thirteen representations below, and the last of each
    // dimension's group is the interface member of ITransformable2D / ITransformable3D.

    // Rotate a 2D shape about the origin.
    Transform(self: IDeformable2D, transform: Rotation2D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Rotate a 2D shape about the origin with a rotor.
    Transform(self: IDeformable2D, transform: Rotor2D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Apply a rigid 2D placement (rotate, then translate).
    Transform(self: IDeformable2D, transform: Pose2D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Apply a 2D TRS transform (scale, rotate, then translate).
    Transform(self: IDeformable2D, transform: TrsTransform2D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Apply a general 2D affine map
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_transformation).
    Transform(self: IDeformable2D, transform: AffineTransform2D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Apply a 2D homography. Precondition: no point of the shape maps onto the
    // line at infinity.
    Transform(self: IDeformable2D, transform: Transform2D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Rotate a 3D shape about the origin.
    Transform(self: IDeformable3D, transform: Quaternion): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Rotate a 3D shape about the origin with a rotor.
    Transform(self: IDeformable3D, transform: Rotor3D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Apply a rigid 3D placement (rotate, then translate).
    Transform(self: IDeformable3D, transform: Pose3D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Apply a rigid motion in motor (dual-quaternion) form.
    Transform(self: IDeformable3D, transform: Motor3D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Apply a 3D TRS transform (scale, rotate, then translate).
    Transform(self: IDeformable3D, transform: TrsTransform3D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));

    // Apply a general 3D affine map.
    Transform(self: IDeformable3D, transform: AffineTransform3D): Self
        => self.Deform(p => p.Transform(transform));
```
